She's not wrong. After all, the wage gap (at least the 77 cents on the dollar one) is just the average pay of all full time working men vs full time working women (ie comparing secretaries to oil rig workers or teachers vs engineers). So the easiest way to close that gap would be for women to pursue higher paying jobs or work longer hours (men typically work more than 40 hours per week on average while women work less than 40 hours per week on average).
The wage gap exists, and they control for types of occupations. They will compare the people working the same job, and women still make less.

That's true, but the gap is typically reduced to around 2-7% instead of something like 23-35%. In those studies, that 2-7% is unexplained (ie, it could be due to discrimination, but it could be due to other unknown factors as well, hence unexplained). One such study is the CONSAD report that was prepared for the US department of labour. However, most of the wage gap (in the 77 cents on the dollar one) can be explained by different choices men and women make, therefore, it makes sense that if we would like to shrink that gap, the easiest way would be for women to make different choices (such as going into high paying trades, becoming engineers, etc).

http://www.consad.com/content/reports/Gender%20Wage%20Gap%20Final%20Report.pdf
